title: Not relevant example in the documentation "Using the Session" - "State Management"
body:
quote from "SQLAlchemy ORM" - "Using the Session" - [State Management](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/master/doc/build/orm/session_state_management.rst)

```python
>>> a1 = Address(id=existing_a1.id, user_id=u1.id)
>>> assert a1.user is None
True
>>> a1 = session.merge(a1)
>>> session.commit()
sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError: (IntegrityError) address.user_id
may not be NULL
```
> Here, we accessed a1.user, which returned its default value
of ``None``, which as a result of this access, has been placed in the ``__dict__`` of
our object ``a1``

Pay attention for **has been placed in `__dict__`**

**Actual behavior**: `IntegrityError` wasn't raised

**The reason is**:

Quote from [What’s New in SQLAlchemy 1.4? change-4519](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/changelog/migration_14.html#change-4519)

> Up until version 1.0 of SQLAlchemy, the behavior of this initialization system for both scalar attributes as well as collections would be that the None or empty collection would be populated into the object’s state, e.g. `__dict__`.
> 
> In version 1.0 as part of [Changes to attribute events and other operations regarding attributes that have no pre-existing value](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/changelog/migration_10.html#migration-3061), this behavior was refined so that the `None` value was no longer populated into `__dict__`, **only returned**.

More details in [What’s New in SQLAlchemy 1.0? migration-3061](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/changelog/migration_10.html#migration-3061)

**As a result** if we run code from documentation:
```python
>>> import sqlalchemy
>>> sqlalchemy.__version__
'1.4.0b1'
>>> 
>>> from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
>>> from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, relationship
>>> from sqlalchemy import create_engine
>>> from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, ForeignKey
>>> 
>>> Base = declarative_base()
>>> 
>>> class User(Base):
...     __tablename__ = 'user'
...     id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
...     name = Column(String(50), nullable=False)
...     addresses = relationship("Address", backref="user")
... 
>>> class Address(Base):
...     __tablename__ = 'address'
...     id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
...     email_address = Column(String(50), nullable=False)
...     user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('user.id'), nullable=False)
... 
>>> engine = create_engine('sqlite:///:memory:', echo=False)
>>> Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
>>> Session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
>>> session = Session()
>>> 
>>> u1 = User(name='ed', addresses=[Address(email_address='ed@ed.com')])
>>> session.add(u1)
>>> session.commit()
>>> 
>>> existing_a1 = u1.addresses[0]
>>> a1 = Address(id=existing_a1.id, user_id=u1.id)
>>> assert a1.user is None
>>> print(a1.user)
None
>>> print(a1.__dict__)
{'_sa_instance_state': <sqlalchemy.orm.state.InstanceState object at 0x7f793c1e0550>, 'id': 1, 'user_id': 1}
>>> 
>>> a1 = session.merge(a1)
>>> session.commit()
>>> 
>>> 
```

**P.S.** I do not know how to fix this example correctly.
